1.why: Reset tokens are stored server-side per session and both /api/reset-validate and /api/password-update strictly compare the submitted token to that session's stored resetToken, so a code only works for its issuing session/account.

2.why: False — another session has no (or a different) resetToken, so a code issued for one session's mock-account reset fails validation for any other user.

3.why: True — password-update mutates only the current session's flags and nothing revokes other entries in the sessions map, so any previously authenticated session keeps working until its 30-minute TTL.

4.why: HTTPS is mandatory (Bun.serve TLS, HSTS header, HTTP port returns 426), but no TLS version is pinned in the config so 'latest TLS version' cannot be confirmed.

5.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed at cost 12 and tokens are generated with crypto.getRandomValues, but reset codes and session user data sit in plaintext in memory rather than being encrypted.

6.why: No real email is sent — delivery is simulated locally containing only the code plus 'never share' warnings, and responses are uniform so no private account data leaks through the message.

7.why: The server validates email format, password policy, and token equality, caps JSON bodies at 4096 bytes, and the client renders all dynamic content via textContent/DOM APIs with no injection sink.

8.why: There are no redirects at all — navigation is restricted to a whitelist of client-side screens, CSP sets form-action 'self', and only same-origin fetches are made.

9.why: The simulated delivery/log messages are static strings with the token inserted via textContent, and no user input is ever rendered as HTML or script (nonce-based CSP with default-src 'none').

10.why: Error responses are generic, but the on-page panel literally labeled 'Logs' deliberately displays the reset code and MFA code, so tokens are shown in logs.

11.why: Passwords are handled well (bcrypt hash kept only in session), but a secret code is stored in the code: const MFA_CODE = "482913" is hardcoded at the top of the source.

12.why: No default username/password credentials exist (there is no login), but the fixed hardcoded MFA code effectively ships a default shared credential.

13.why: Per-session rate limiters return 429 after 3 reset requests, 5 code guesses, or 5 MFA attempts per 15 minutes, barring repeated wrong attempts.

14.why: Although reset-request responses are uniform, the delivered token is returned to any requester and reset-validate succeeds only for the mock account, so account existence can be inferred through that oracle.

15.why: The reset code is a 32-byte CSPRNG base64url token, single-use with a 15-minute expiry, and bound to the requesting session's recovery of the specific account.
